{{Quote|The elix inhabited a forest world about to be destroyed by a supernova explosion.|Obo Rin, ''Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy'', Revised Edition|<ref name="GG42" />}}
A '''forest world''' with 1.1 standard [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the small [[Bird/Legends|birds]] of [[Diet/Legends|prey]] known as the [[elix]]. At some point during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the [[Forest/Legends|forest]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] was about to be destroyed by a [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]]. Hoping to save the elix from extinction, a group of zealous planetary [[Ecologist/Legends|ecologists]] transplanted the [[Species/Legends|species]] to [[Dar'Or]], an [[Waza|arboreal]] planet located in the [[Jospro sector/Legends|Jospro sector]]<ref name="GG42" /> of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref>

The ecologists, however, overlooked the fact that the new home of the elix had lower gravity, which led to the avians becoming powerful and fast apex predators that threatened the native [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]], the [[Ri'Dar]]. [[Standard year/Legends|Years]] after the transplantation of the elix from their doomed homeworld, the [[sentientologist]] [[Obo Rin]] mentioned that forested world in an entry of his publication, ''[[Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy]]'', dedicated to the Ri'Dar.<ref name="GG42" />

==Behind the scenes==
The homeworld of the elix was first mentioned in ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', a [[1989]] sourcebook authored by [[Troy Denning]] for use with [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="GG41">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref>
